questions.question: Which chemical species is being oxidized in the following chemical reaction? CuO+H₂→Cu+H₂O
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**H₂**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the reaction CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, hydrogen (H₂) is the species that is being oxidized.
 
• Oxidation is defined as the loss of electrons. In this reaction, H₂ loses electrons and forms H₂O.
 
• CuO is being reduced to Cu, which means it gains electrons.
 
• Oxidation and reduction always occur simultaneously in a redox reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidation:**

 
 
• Oxidation is a chemical reaction that involves the loss of electrons by a molecule, atom, or ion.
 
• It often involves the addition of oxygen or the removal of hydrogen.
 
• For example, in the reaction above, H₂ is oxidized to H₂O.
 
 
 
• **Reduction:**
 
 
• Reduction is the gain of electrons by a molecule, atom, or ion.
 
• It often involves the removal of oxygen or the addition of hydrogen.
 
• In the reaction above, CuO is reduced to Cu.
 
 
 
• **Redox Reactions:**
 
 
• Redox (reduction-oxidation) reactions are chemical reactions in which the oxidation states of atoms are changed.
 
• These reactions involve the transfer of electrons between two chemical species.
 
• One species gets oxidized (loses electrons), and the other gets reduced (gains electrons).
 
 
 
• **Oxidizing Agent:**
 
 
• An oxidizing agent, or oxidant, is a substance that has the ability to oxidize other substances (cause them to lose electrons).
 
• In the reaction above, CuO acts as the oxidizing agent because it accepts electrons from H₂.
 
 
 
• **Reducing Agent:**
 
 
• A reducing agent, or reductant, is a substance that has the ability to reduce other substances (cause them to gain electrons).
 
• In the reaction above, H₂ acts as the reducing agent because it donates electrons to CuO.

questions.question: Double displacement reactions usually occur in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**aqueous solution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Double displacement reactions generally occur in **aqueous solutions**.
 
• In such reactions, two compounds in aqueous solution exchange ions to form two new compounds.
 
• These reactions often result in the formation of a precipitate, gas, or water.
 
• Examples include the reaction between silver nitrate and sodium chloride in water, forming silver chloride precipitate and sodium nitrate in solution.
 
• The solubility of the reactants and products in water plays a crucial role in these reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Precipitate:**

 
 
• A solid that forms and settles out of a liquid mixture as a result of a chemical reaction.
 
• Common in double displacement reactions where insoluble salts are formed.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Double Displacement Reactions:**
 
 
• Reaction of barium chloride with sulfuric acid to form barium sulfate precipitate and hydrochloric acid.
 
• Reaction of sodium carbonate with calcium chloride to form calcium carbonate precipitate and sodium chloride.
 
 
 
• **Solubility Rules:**
 
 
• Guidelines that help predict whether a compound will dissolve in water.
 
• Important for determining the products of double displacement reactions.
 
 
 
• **Formation of Gas:**
 
 
• In some double displacement reactions, a gas may be formed as a product.
 
• Example: Reaction between hydrochloric acid and sodium sulfite to form sodium chloride, water, and sulfur dioxide gas.

questions.question: The chemical reaction in which a substance produces heat by reacting with oxygen,
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Combustion**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The chemical reaction in which a substance produces heat by reacting with oxygen is known as **combustion**.
 
• Combustion reactions are exothermic, meaning they release heat.
 
• In a typical combustion reaction, a hydrocarbon reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide, water, and heat.
 
• Combustion is utilized in various applications including heating, power generation, and propulsion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidation** is a broader term that refers to the loss of electrons by a molecule, atom, or ion.
 
• **Fragmentation** involves breaking a molecule into smaller pieces.
 
• **Respiratory** processes involve the exchange of gases in living organisms.
 
• Combustion is a specific type of oxidation reaction that involves oxygen and produces heat and light.

questions.question: What type of reaction takes place when calcium oxide reacts vigorously with water to produce slaked lime?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Combination reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A combination reaction occurs when two or more substances combine to form a single product.
 
• When calcium oxide (CaO) reacts with water (H₂O), it forms calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂), also known as slaked lime.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂.
 
• This reaction is exothermic, meaning it releases a significant amount of heat.
 
• Combination reactions are also known as synthesis reactions because they involve the formation of a new compound from simpler substances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposition reaction**

 
 
• A decomposition reaction occurs when a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• For example, the decomposition of water into hydrogen and oxygen gases: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂.
 
 
 
• **Double displacement reaction**
 
 
• In a double displacement reaction, the ions of two compounds exchange places in an aqueous solution to form two new compounds.
 
• An example is the reaction between sodium chloride and silver nitrate: NaCl + AgNO₃ → NaNO₃ + AgCl.
 
 
 
• **Displacement reaction**
 
 
• A displacement reaction occurs when an element reacts with a compound, displacing another element from it.
 
• For instance, when zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂.

questions.question:
Which of the following is(are) an endothermic process(es)?

(i) Dilution of sulphuric acid

(ii) Sublimation of dry ice

(iii) Condensation of water vapours

(iv) Evaporation of water
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• Every change involves the involvement of energy transformations.
 
• The process in which the absorption of heat energy happens is named as an endoergic process.

Explanation:__

 
• The dilution of any strong acid can be done by adding the strong acid to water.
 
• Then, the hydrogen bonds present in the acid break and release heat energy. 
 
• This change is an example of exothermic change.
 
• **Sublimation **is the change where a solid changes into its gaseous state.
 
• During this change, energy is absorbed.
 
• Hence, this is an example of an **endothermic process.**
 
• Condensation of water vapours to water releases heat energy.
 
• This is an exothermic process.
 
• **Evaporation** of water is a process in which heat energy is absorbed.

**So, this is an example of an endothermic process.**

questions.question: Reflect on the impact of chemical changes in our daily lives, from cooking and digestion to industrial manufacturing. Discuss how these changes are essential for transforming raw materials into usable products, supporting modern conveniences and life processes.

options.text: Chemical changes have no real applications
Chemical changes are fundamental to life and industry
Only physical changes have practical applications

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Chemical changes are fundamental to life and industry.**

**__Concept:-__**

__
 
• **Transformation of Substances: **Chemical changes involve the transformation of initial substances (reactants) into new substances (products) with different chemical and physical properties.
 
• **Role of Catalysts:** Many essential chemical changes, both in nature and industry, are facilitated by catalysts, which speed up reactions without being consumed in the process.
 
• **Energy Involvement:** Chemical changes often involve the release or absorption of energy, which can be harnessed for various uses, such as heat during combustion or electrical energy in batteries.
 
• **Synthesis and Decomposition: **These changes enable the synthesis of complex chemicals from simpler substances or the breakdown of complex materials into their constituent components, both of which are crucial for a myriad of applications.

**Explanation:-__**

Chemical changes are at the heart of countless processes that support modern life, conveniences, and essential biological functions. Far from being detrimental or irrelevant, chemical changes enable the transformation of materials into new substances with different properties, which is indispensable in various contexts from cooking to industrial manufacturing.

__
 
• **Cooking:** When we cook food, chemical changes occur that alter the food's nutritional properties, taste, texture, and appearance. For example, the Maillard reaction, which occurs when proteins and sugars react under heat, is responsible for the browning and flavor development in baked goods and grilled meats. These changes not only make our food more enjoyable but also can make it more digestible and safe to eat by eliminating harmful bacteria.
 
• **Digestion: **Digestion is a series of chemical changes where the complex molecules in our food are broken down into simpler substances that our bodies can absorb. Enzymes play a key role in these processes, catalyzing the breakdown of proteins, carbohydrates, and fats into amino acids, sugars, and fatty acids, respectively. Without these chemical changes, we would not be able to extract the essential nutrients our bodies require to function.
 
• **Industrial Manufacturing: **Chemical changes are critical in transforming raw materials into a vast array of products. For example, the Haber-Bosch process combines nitrogen from the air with hydrogen to synthesize ammonia, a key ingredient in fertilizers that support agriculture worldwide. Chemical synthesis creates pharmaceuticals, plastics, fuels, and many other products that we rely on every day.
 
• **Pollution Control and Environmental Management: **Through chemical changes, harmful pollutants can be neutralized or transformed into less harmful substances. Treatment of wastewater involves chemical processes that remove or break down pollutants, ensuring that water returned to the environment doesn't harm ecosystems

**Conclusion:-__**

So, the correct statement is Chemical changes are fundamental to life and industry.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements in view of rusting of Iron :

A. It is chemically named as Iron Oxide.

B. Rusting is considered as a chemical change.

C. Zinc is coated on iron articles to prevent them from rusting.

Choose the correct answer :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** A, B and C **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Statement A. True ​

 
• When iron is exposed to moist air, a reddish-brown coating of hydrated Iron (III) Oxide (Fe2O3) is deposited on its surface.
 
• This reddish-brown coating is called rust.
 
• **Rust is chemically known as iron oxide (Fe2O3).**
 
• Rust is an iron oxide, which occurs when iron or an alloy that contains iron, like steel, is exposed to oxygen and moisture for a long period of time.

Statement B. True 

 
• **Rusting is indeed a chemical change.**
 
• In a chemical change, the substance undergoing the change is fundamentally transformed into a different substance.
 
• When iron rusts, the iron atoms react with oxygen atoms in the air and produce a completely new substance, iron oxide.
 
• This transformation cannot be reversed by simple physical means, which is a characteristic of chemical changes.

Statement C. True 

 
• The process of** coating iron or steel with zinc is known as galvanization.**
 
• Zinc, being more reactive than iron, oxidizes first and forms a **protective layer of zinc oxide over the iron article.**
 
• This layer prevents the iron from coming into contact with oxygen and water, thus **preventing rusting.**
 
• This process is widely used to protect iron and steel products, like nails, car bodies, and roofing, from corrosion.

questions.question: Why does silver chloride turn white in sunlight?

options.text: Due to rusting of silver in the presence of oxygen
Due to decomposition of silver chloride into silver and chlorine by light.
Due to displacement of silver chloride into silver oxide

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Due to decomposition of silver chloride into silver and chlorine by light.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Silver chloride** is a **photosensitive compound**, which means it reacts to light by decomposing.
 
• When silver chloride is exposed to sunlight, the **energy from the light** causes the** compound to break down into silver and chlorine ions.**
 
• The s**ilver ions combine with other substances** in the environment to **form a white precipitate**, which gives the **appearance of the silver chloride turning white**.
 
• This process is reversible, and the white precipitate can turn back into silver chloride when removed from sunlight.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Application of this phenomenon**:

 
 
• As this process is reversible, as the grey color can fade when the silver chloride is shielded from light or heated.
 
• This property has **historical significance in photography**, as it was **used in the early photographic process known as the daguerreotype**.
 
 
 
• **Redox reaction:**
 
 
• **Redox reactions are chemical processes involving oxidation and reduction in which the oxidation states of the reactants change.** 
 
• In a chemical reaction, the **material that is being reduced **is referred to as the** oxidizing agent**, and the **substance that is being oxidized** is referred to as the **reducing agent**. 
 
 
 
• **Displacement reaction:**
 
 
• **When an atom in a molecule is displaced by another atom, this is known as a displacement reaction.**

questions.question:
In the given reaction, the oxidation state of Mn are

3MnO₄ ²⁻ + 4H⁺ → 2MnO₄⁻ + MnO₂ + 2H₂O
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Oxidation state**

__
 
• The oxidation state of an atom can be defined as **the hypothetical charge that would be held by that atom** if all of its bonds to other atoms were completely ionic in nature.
 
• Oxidation state and oxidation number are terms frequently used interchangeably.
 
• They are the quantities that describe the number of electrons lost in an atom. Ideally, the oxidation state is either **zero, positive, or negative**.

 

**Given data and Calculation:**__

3MnO4 2- + 4H+ → 2MnO4- + MnO2 + 2H2O

In MnO4 2- , let oxidation state of Mn is x.

x + (-2 × 4 ) = -2 , x = +6

In MnO4 - , let oxidation state of Mn is x.

x + (-2 × 4 ) = -1 , x = +7

In MnO2, let oxidation state of Mn is x.

x + (-2 × 2 ) = 0, x = +4

So the oxidation state of Mn are **+4, +6, +7 only.**

questions.question:
In the given reaction, reduction of which substance takes place?

Fe₂O₃(s) + 2Al(s) → Al₂O₃(s) + 2Fe(l)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ferric oxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ferric oxide (Fe₂O₃) is reduced in the reaction.**

 
 
• Reduction is the gain of electrons or decrease in oxidation state.
 
• Iron's oxidation state in Fe₂O₃ is +3.
 
• Iron's oxidation state in Fe is 0.
 
• The decrease from +3 to 0 shows iron gained electrons.
 
• Fe₂O₃ gains electrons, so it is reduced.
 
• Oxygen is removed from the iron oxide.
 
• This is a redox reaction.
 
• Fe₂O₃ reduction is important in iron production.
 
• The reaction is exothermic.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aluminum (Al) is oxidized.**
 
• Oxidation is the loss of electrons or increase in oxidation state.
 
• Aluminum's oxidation state in Al is 0.
 
• Aluminum's oxidation state in Al₂O₃ is +3.
 
• The increase from 0 to +3 shows aluminum lost electrons.
 
• Aluminum loses electrons, so it is oxidized.
 
• Aluminum is the reducing agent.
 
• Al₂O₃ formation drives the reaction.
 
• Aluminum oxide (Al₂O₃) is a product, not reduced.
 
• It's a stable compound.
 
• It's the result of the oxidation reaction.
 
• Iron (Fe) is a product, not reduced.
 
• It's the elemental form of iron.
 
• It's the result of the reduction reaction.

• When methane burns, **CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.**
 
• When methane burns in presence of air or oxygen, it produces a large amount of heat, along with **carbon dioxide and water vapour** formation. 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Methane is a chemical compound **with the chemical formula **CH₄** (one atom of carbon and four atoms of hydrogen).
 
• It is a **group-14 hydride** and the simplest alkane and is the main constituent of natural gas.
 
• **The largest reservoir of methane** is under the seafloor in the form of methane clathrates.
 
• When **methane** **reaches** the **surface** and the **atmosphere**, it is known as **atmospheric methane.**

questions.question: Which of the following processes is NOT an example of physical change
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Photosynthesis**.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The dissolution of **salt in water **is a **physical change.**
 
• Because salt can be obtained again by **making water vapor**.
 
• As a result,** no new substance is formed**, called physical changes.
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants transform solar energy into chemical energy. During photosynthesis in green plants, light energy is captured and used to convert water, carbon dioxide, and minerals into oxygen and energy.
 
• In Photosynthesis, Solar energy is converted into chemical energy.
 
• **Photosynthesis is not a physical process**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​Physical change -**

 
 
• Under this, there is **no change in the chemical nature** or chemical identity of the substance.
 
• For example, after pouring water on a utensil and heating it from below, the water turns into vapor, if you keep a lid on that utensil, then that vapor again converts into the water, this is a kind of physical change.
 
 
 
• **Chemical changes -**
 
 
• Under this, the structure of matter changes.
 
• One or more substances combine or break down to form new substances.
 
• Its properties and characteristics change

questions.question: What is the method of balancing chemical equations called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Hit and trial method**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **hit and trial method **is a common and straightforward technique used to balance chemical equations. The goal is to ensure that there are the same number of each type of atom on both sides of the equation, in accordance with the Law of Conservation of Mass.
 
• This method involves adjusting the coefficients of reactants and products by trial and error until the number of atoms of each element is balanced on both sides of the equation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Molar Method**

 
 
• The Molar method involves using the mole concept to balance chemical equations.
 
• It ensures that the number of moles of each element is equal on both sides of the equation.
 
• This method is often used in stoichiometry problems.
 
• It is particularly useful for reactions involving gases where volumes are involved.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Method**
 
 
• This term is not commonly used to describe a specific method for balancing chemical equations.
 
• It may refer to any general approach used to balance chemical equations.
 
• Typically, it would involve ensuring that the number of atoms of each element is equal on both sides of the equation.
 
 
 
• **Hit and Trial Method**
 
 
• The Hit and Trial method involves trial and error to balance chemical equations.
 
• It is often used for simple equations where a systematic approach may not be necessary.
 
• This method can be time-consuming for complex equations.
 
• It involves adjusting coefficients until the number of atoms of each element is balanced on both sides of the equation.

questions.question:
Identify the following type of reaction.

NaCl (aq) + AgNO₃(aq) → AgCl(s) + NaNO₃(aq)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Double displacement reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

** Double Displacement Reaction**

__
 
• **Definition:** Involves the exchange of ions between two compounds.
 
• **General Form:** AB + CD → AD + CB
 
 
• Where A and C are cations (positively charged ions)
 
• B and D are anions (negatively charged ions)
 
 
 
• **Key Features:**
 
 
• Often occurs in aqueous solutions.
 
• May result in the formation of a precipitate (solid), a gas, or water.
 
• Example:
 
 
• **Precipitation:** BaCl2 (aq) + Na2SO4 (aq) → BaSO4 (s) + 2NaCl (aq)
 
 
• Barium chloride reacts with sodium sulfate to form insoluble barium sulfate (precipitate) and soluble sodium chloride.
 
 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Combination Reaction**

 
• **Definition:** Two or more substances combine to form a single, more complex product.
 
• **General Form:** A + B → AB
 
• **Key Features:**
 
 
• Often involves the formation of a compound from its elements.
 
• Can also involve the combination of two compounds to form a more complex one.
 
• Example:
 
 
• **Formation of water:** 2H2 (g) + O2 (g) → 2H2O (l)
 
 
• Hydrogen gas reacts with oxygen gas to form liquid water.
 
 
 
 
 
 

**Decomposition Reaction**

 
• **Definition:** A single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• **General Form:** AB → A + B
 
• **Key Features:**
 
 
• Often requires an input of energy, such as heat or light.
 
• Examples:
 
 
• **Electrolysis of water:** 2H2O (l) → 2H2 (g) + O2 (g)
 
 
• Water decomposes into hydrogen and oxygen gas in the presence of an electric current.
 
 
 
• **Thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate:** CaCO3 (s) → CaO (s) + CO2 (g)
 
 
• Calcium carbonate decomposes into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide when heated.
 
 
 
 
 
 

**Combustion Reaction**

 
• **Definition:** A rapid reaction that involves the combination of a substance with oxygen, usually releasing heat and light.
 
• **General Form:** Fuel + Oxygen → Carbon dioxide + Water + Heat + Light
 
• **Key Features:**
 
 
• Often involves the burning of organic compounds (hydrocarbons).
 
• Examples:
 
 
• **Burning of methane:** CH4 (g) + 2O2 (g) → CO2 (g) + 2H2O (l) + Heat + Light
 
 
• Methane reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide, water, heat, and light.
